bug_semantics: RandR RRChangeProviderProperty computes int total_size = total_len * size_in_bytes (size_in_bytes = format>>3) with no overflow guard, then malloc(total_size) and memcpy of len/prop_value->size times size_in_bytes. A local X client can issue RRChangeProviderProperty (ProcRRChangeProviderProperty) with format 8/16/32 and a large nUnits, or Append/Prepend onto an existing property so total_len = prop_value->size + len, wrapping the 32-bit int allocation size. The wrapped malloc is smaller than the subsequent copies, causing heap overflow (CWE-190) that Red Hat rates as memory corruption / possible code execution.
flaw_origin: The unchecked multiply-and-malloc was first written when Dave Airlie added RandR provider objects and provider properties, cloning the existing RRChangeOutputProperty allocation pattern into the new RRChangeProviderProperty in randr/rrproviderproperty.c. That commit created the file and the client request path; the overflow check was never present until the 2025 CVE fix.
